issues.body:
The diff correctly rewrites the sibling comment in this file (line ~36) and both bench.yml sites, but the same false claim survives at scripts/ci-close-merged-beads.py:42:

  # The default GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push to protected `main` (GH013, empty bypass list — see
  # bead-autoclose.yml's history, sq-roe3), and a PR-based write is equally dead from that

This is the identical assertion the PR exists to retract, in a tracked and currently-executed script, and it explicitly cross-references this workflow's history -- so the two comments now disagree with each other about the same ruleset fact. Round 2 flagged this claim class as a NIT; round 3 recorded it fixed on the strength of a grep scoped to docs/ compliance/ .github/workflows/, which cannot reach scripts/.

Not a blocker: the comment makes no wrong behavioral claim (GITHUB_TOKEN is indeed not the administrator role, so it is still GH013-rejected, and the issue-native close path the comment goes on to describe is unaffected). It is a doc-honesty leftover, and leaving it means a future reader can still cite "empty bypass list" from a file in main.
issues.fix_hint: In scripts/ci-close-merged-beads.py:42, mirror the wording already adopted in bead-autoclose.yml -- e.g. "(GH013; only the repository-administrator role can bypass, not GITHUB_TOKEN — see bead-autoclose.yml's history, sq-roe3)". Then re-run the verification grep with scripts/ IN scope so the sweep is provably complete, e.g.: grep -rn -iE 'empty bypass|bypass_actors: \[\]|no admin bypass|current_user_can_bypass' --include='*.md' --include='*.yml' --include='*.py' --include='*.sh' docs/ compliance/ .github/ scripts/ research/ (expect zero hits; .beads/issues.jsonl is an intentional historical archive and should stay excluded).
issues.title: Retraction of the "empty bypass list" claim is incomplete: one site remains in scripts/ci-close-merged-beads.py:42

verdict.summary:
Doc/comment-only change (no code, tests, or runtime surface) retracting the false "empty bypass_actors / current_user_can_bypass: never" claim and recording the live state: one RepositoryRole bypass actor (actor_id: 5, bypass_mode: always) plus a merge_queue row in the live-rules table.

PROGRESS LABEL: the head is UNCHANGED since round 3 (still a1ff0ec3; no round-3 fix commit), so the artifact is byte-identical to the one round 3 approved. Nothing regressed. Hence "stagnant", not "regressing": the finding below is not new damage, it is round-2 NIT #4 ("comments asserting an EMPTY bypass list") only PARTIALLY closed -- round 3's grep was scoped to docs/ compliance/ .github/workflows/ and could not see scripts/.

Verified against the checkout, not just the diff:
- All five round-2 findings remain closed. docs/branch-protection.md:13-15 now agrees with the section it cross-references; the "Other settings", solo-maintainer, compensating-controls and live-rules-table sites are mutually consistent.
- Compliance drift closed at all four cited sites (openssf.md:26, slsa/controls.md:141/:142, slsa/evidence.md:125); the collateral over-claim ("≥1 approving review, require-code-owners, dismiss-stale") now matches the enforced 0/false/false reality.
- No "emergency bypass" phrasing survives anywhere.
- actor_id: 5 for RepositoryRole is the documented admin role id, so the identification is correct. The live ruleset is out-of-repo and unverifiable from a read-only checkout -- exactly why these stay AR, not IV.
- The merge_queue row (ALLGREEN / max_entries_to_merge: 8 / 60 min) matches §Omnibus batching at lines 452-455.
- research/orchestration-private-registry-worker.md:140,257 ("the App is not on any bypass list") stay TRUE under an admin-only bypass list -- not drift. .beads/issues.jsonl:57-58 quote the old text inside CLOSED bead records; correctly left alone.

One residual site remains in a tracked, active script (below): comment-only, so it does not block.
